questions.question:
Read the below statements:

1. The Solicitor General of India is appointed by the President.

2. A contestant for the President of India must deposit ₹15,000 as security.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statement 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** "The Solicitor General of India is appointed by the President."

 
 
• The **Solicitor General of India** is the second-highest law officer of the country, assisting the **Attorney General of India**.
 
• While the **Attorney General of India is appointed by the President** under **Article 76(1)** of the Constitution, the Solicitor General is not a constitutional post.
 
• The Solicitor General, along with Additional Solicitors General, is appointed by the **Central Government** and not directly by the President. This appointment is made under the authority of the **Law Officers (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1987**.
 
• *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** "A contestant for the President of India must deposit ₹15,000 as security."
 
 
• According to the **Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952**, a person contesting the election for the office of the **President of India** must deposit a sum of **₹15,000** as security.
 
• This security deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to secure at least **one-sixth of the total valid votes polled**.
 
• This provision ensures that only serious candidates participate in the election process.
 
• *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solicitor General of India:**

 
 
• The Solicitor General is the second law officer after the Attorney General of India and represents the Union of India in the Supreme Court.
 
• Unlike the Attorney General, the Solicitor General is not a constitutional post but is appointed under statutory provisions.
 
• The Solicitor General assists the Attorney General in performing official duties and represents the government in cases assigned by the Supreme Court or High Courts.
 
• The Solicitor General is appointed by the **Central Government** on the advice of the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)**.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria and Security Deposit for Presidential Elections:**
 
 
• A candidate contesting the election for the post of the President of India must fulfill specific eligibility criteria as laid down in **Articles 58 and 59** of the Constitution of India.
 
• **Eligibility Requirements:**
 
 
• The candidate must be a citizen of India.
 
• The candidate must be at least **35 years** old.
 
• The candidate must be qualified to become a member of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The candidate must not hold any office of profit under the Government of India, state government, or public authority.
 
 
 
• The security deposit of **₹15,000** ensures that frivolous candidates do not contest the Presidential election.
 
• The deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to secure at least **one-sixth of the total valid votes polled**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Solicitor General:**

 
 
• The Solicitor General is not eligible to participate in parliamentary proceedings.
 
• The role of the Solicitor General is limited to advising the government and representing it in courts.
 
• The Solicitor General does not have executive authority like the Attorney General.
 
 
 
• **Presidential Elections:**
 
 
• The election of the President of India is conducted by the Election Commission of India through a process of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• The voters in this election include the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and Union territories with Legislative Assemblies.
 
 

60:T

questions.question:
Based on the given statements, choose the correct answer:

Statement I: Mathura art catered to both Indian and foreign devotees.

Statement II: Mathura art avoided depicting themes inspired by nature.

Which option is correct?

options.text: Both I and II are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I is correct.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I:** Mathura art catered to both Indian and foreign devotees.

 
 
• The **Mathura School of Art** was one of the prominent artistic traditions of ancient India. It thrived during the **Kushan period** (1st century BCE–3rd century CE).
 
• This art form represented a synthesis of **Indian and foreign influences**, particularly Greek and Central Asian styles. It served the needs of both **domestic and international devotees**.
 
• Mathura art focused heavily on **Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu themes**, creating sculptures and carvings that appealed to the religious sentiments of a diverse audience. These included foreign merchants and travelers influenced by Indian spirituality. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement II:** Mathura art avoided depicting themes inspired by nature.
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**. Mathura art frequently included **naturalistic themes** in its sculptures and carvings. These depictions included **animals, plants, trees, floral motifs, and celestial beings**, showcasing the connection between religion and nature.
 
• For example, sculptures of the **Bodhi tree** (symbolizing enlightenment) and animals such as lions and elephants were common, reflecting the importance of nature in religious symbolism. *Hence, statement II is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Only I is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mathura Art:**

 
 
• Mathura art originated in **Mathura, Uttar Pradesh**, and flourished during the reign of the **Kushan rulers**. It is considered a blend of **indigenous Indian traditions** and **foreign influences**.
 
• It primarily focused on creating sculptures of **Buddha, Jain Tirthankaras, and Hindu deities**. This art style contributed significantly to the development of **Indian iconography**.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics:**
 
 
• Mathura art used **red sandstone** as its primary material and featured **naturalistic and symbolic depictions**.
 
• The sculptures often depicted **human figures with rounded faces, prominent eyes, and smiling expressions**, emphasizing emotional warmth.
 
• It played a crucial role in the spread of **Buddhism and Jainism** across India and abroad through artistic representations.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Influence:**
 
 
• Mathura art incorporated elements of **Greco-Bactrian art**, evident in the **styling of sculptures and motifs**.
 
• The **cultural exchange** between Indian and foreign traditions enriched the diversity of Mathura art.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Gandhara Art:**

 
 
• **Gandhara art**, another prominent tradition, was heavily influenced by **Greek and Roman styles**, emphasizing realism and intricate details.
 
• Unlike Mathura art, Gandhara sculptures used **grey schist stone** and focused on realistic human anatomy.
 
• Both styles played a role in spreading **Buddhist art**, but Mathura art retained stronger indigenous features.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Mathura Art:**
 
 
• The legacy of Mathura art is evident in the development of later Indian artistic traditions such as **Gupta art**, which combined aesthetic beauty with spiritual symbolism.
 
• Mathura continues to be a significant center for **religious tourism and cultural studies**.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Hola Mohalla festival of Punjab?

options.text: Celebrated mainly by women for crafts and folk songs in Patiala
Known for martial displays, langars and mock battles by Nihangs at Anandpur Sahib
A harvest festival celebrated before Diwali
Observed on the same day as Holi

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Known for martial displays, langars and mock battles by Nihangs at Anandpur Sahib.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hola Mohalla** is a significant Sikh festival celebrated annually, primarily in **Anandpur Sahib**, Punjab.
 
• The festival showcases martial arts, mock battles, and other traditional warrior skills performed by the **Nihang Sikhs**, who are known for their distinctive blue robes and martial history.
 
• It also features **langars** (community kitchens), where free meals are served to thousands of devotees and visitors during the celebrations.
 
• The event typically includes processions, recitation of religious hymns, and cultural performances, emphasizing the rich heritage of Sikhism. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• Statement 1 (celebrated by women for crafts and folk songs in Patiala) is incorrect because Hola Mohalla is not specifically associated with women-centric activities or crafts in Patiala.
 
• Statement 3 (a harvest festival celebrated before Diwali) is also incorrect. Hola Mohalla is not a harvest festival; it typically occurs a day after the Hindu festival of **Holi**.
 
• Statement 4 (observed on the same day as Holi) is incorrect because Hola Mohalla usually takes place **a day after Holi**, not on the same day. *Hence, the correct answer is the second statement.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Significance of Hola Mohalla:**

 
 
• The festival was initiated by **Guru Gobind Singh**, the tenth Sikh Guru, in the late 17th century. It was meant to instill martial spirit and courage among the Sikh community.
 
• The term **‘Hola Mohalla’** is derived from ‘Hola,’ which means a military charge, and ‘Mohalla,’ meaning a gathering or an organized procession.
 
 
 
• **Celebrations and Features:**
 
 
• The event includes activities like **mock battles**, sword fighting, horse riding, and Gatka (a traditional Sikh martial art).
 
• It also features religious and cultural processions, kirtans (devotional music), and poetry recitals.
 
• The festival is deeply rooted in Sikh values of bravery, unity, and community service.
 
 
 
• **Important Locations:**
 
 
• **Anandpur Sahib**, the birthplace of the Khalsa (the collective body of initiated Sikhs), is the focal point of Hola Mohalla celebrations.
 
• Other places in Punjab also observe the festival, but Anandpur Sahib is the most renowned for its grand celebrations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cultural and Religious Impact:**

 
 
• Hola Mohalla serves as an occasion to remember the Sikh community’s martial traditions and to inspire younger generations to uphold these values.
 
• The festival is an excellent example of Sikhism’s emphasis on community bonding, equality, and selfless service through activities like **langars**.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Popularity:**
 
 
• The festival attracts thousands of visitors, including tourists from across India and abroad, making it a major cultural and religious event in Punjab.
 
• It is also recognized for its vibrant atmosphere and the participants’ colorful traditional attire, adding to its appeal.

questions.question: Mārgi Sangita in ancient Indian music was primarily associated with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vedic musical heritage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mārgi Sangita** refers to the ancient tradition of Indian classical music that has its roots in the **Vedic era**. It is associated with the music that was performed in religious and spiritual contexts during the Vedic period.
 
• The term "Mārgi" translates to "the path" or "the way," signifying its connection to the sacred and divine purposes. It was considered a pathway to spiritual enlightenment and was primarily used in **Vedic rituals**. This is why it is associated with the **Vedic musical heritage**.
 
• The music in this tradition was highly structured and adhered to strict rules of composition and performance. This reflects the highly disciplined nature of Vedic practices. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• Mārgi Sangita differs from **Desi Sangita**, which is linked to regional and folk traditions. While Mārgi Sangita was connected to spiritual and ritualistic practices, Desi Sangita represented popular or regional music that catered to entertainment and social functions.
 
• Mārgi Sangita laid the foundation for **Indian classical music**, influencing subsequent musical traditions such as **Hindustani** and **Carnatic music**. It is considered the origin of the structured and theoretical frameworks that define classical Indian music today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vedic Musical Heritage:**

 
 
• The **Vedic period** is considered the origin of Indian music. It was during this time that hymns from the **Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda**, and **Atharvaveda** were composed and sung in specific melodic patterns.
 
• The **Samaveda** is particularly important for the development of Indian music, as it contains a collection of hymns meant to be sung during rituals. These hymns were set to musical notations called **Samagana**.
 
• The compositions were highly structured, with specific rules for rhythm, melody, and pitch, which formed the basis for the later development of Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Musical Traditions:**
 
 
• **Folk Singing:** This style is associated with regional, community-based music and does not follow the strict rules of classical traditions. It is used for entertainment, celebrations, and oral storytelling, making it distinct from Mārgi Sangita.

Which of the following correctly describes water bodies in the India Desert?

1. Streams remain perennial throughout the year.

2. Most streams vanish into sandy terrain.

Which is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Desert**, also known as the **Thar Desert**, is characterized by its arid climate and sandy terrain.
 
• The streams in the desert region do not remain perennial throughout the year due to the **extreme arid conditions** and **low rainfall**. Most streams in the Thar Desert are seasonal and dry up during summers. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Most streams in the Indian Desert vanish into the **sandy terrain** due to the porous nature of the sand, which allows water to seep in quickly. This phenomenon is common in arid regions with sandy landscapes. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• Examples of such streams include the **Luni River**, which flows through Rajasthan but eventually disappears into the desert sands.
 
• The presence of **endorheic basins** (closed drainage basins) in the desert region further supports the disappearance of streams into the sandy terrain. *Hence, the correct answer is Only 2.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Desert (Thar Desert):**

 
 
• The **Thar Desert** is located in **northwestern India**, covering parts of **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana**.
 
• It is the **largest desert in India** and the **17th largest desert in the world**, with an area of approximately **200,000 square kilometers**.
 
• The desert experiences **low rainfall**, generally less than **150 mm annually**, and extreme temperatures ranging from **50°C in summers** to **0°C in winters**.
 
 
 
• **Water Characteristics in the Thar Desert:**
 
 
• The desert region has **seasonal rivers**, such as the **Luni River**, which flow only during the monsoon season.
 
• Due to the **porous sandy soil**, water from streams and rivers quickly percolates into the ground, leading to the disappearance of water bodies.
 
• The region lacks perennial water sources, and streams often end in **endorheic basins** or evaporate due to high temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Endorheic Basins:**
 
 
• **Endorheic basins** are closed drainage systems where water does not flow into external water bodies like seas or oceans.
 
• In deserts like the Thar, streams and rivers often end in such basins, where water evaporates or seeps into the ground.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Climate Characteristics:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert has an **arid climate**, with **high evaporation rates** and low humidity levels.
 
• Rainfall is sparse, and vegetation is limited to **xerophytic plants** adapted to survive in dry conditions.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features:**
 
 
• The desert features **dunes**, salt flats, and rocky terrain. Sand dunes cover about **50%** of the desert area.
 
• The soil is largely sandy, which results in the quick absorption of water from streams and rivers.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Water Management:**
 
 
• Water management in desert regions involves creating artificial reservoirs, rainwater harvesting, and groundwater recharge systems.
 
• Projects like the **Indira Gandhi Canal** have been implemented to provide irrigation and drinking water to the desert regions.

questions.question: The term “pleiotropy” refers to:

options.text: Many genes influencing a single trait

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One gene influencing multiple traits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pleiotropy** refers to the phenomenon where a **single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits**. This is a direct outcome of the fact that genes often encode for proteins or enzymes that participate in multiple biochemical pathways or developmental processes.
 
• An example of pleiotropy is observed in genetic disorders like **Sickle Cell Anemia**, where the mutation in the **HBB gene** affects multiple traits, including the shape of red blood cells, oxygen transport efficiency, and susceptibility to various complications.
 
• The term is derived from Greek, where "pleio" means "more" and "tropy" means "change". This indicates the ability of one gene to bring about multiple changes or effects. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• Pleiotropy is significant in understanding genetic diseases, as it highlights how a mutation in one gene can have widespread effects across different body systems. This helps in diagnosing and treating complex genetic disorders.
 
• Examples of pleiotropy include **Marfan Syndrome**, where a mutation in the **FBN1 gene** affects connective tissues, leading to traits like elongated limbs, cardiovascular issues, and eye problems. Similarly, the **PKU (Phenylketonuria)** disorder results from a defect in the **PAH gene**, affecting multiple metabolic and cognitive functions.
 
• In contrast, the term "polygenic inheritance" is used when multiple genes collectively influence a single trait. This is different from pleiotropy and applies to traits like height, skin color, and eye color. *Hence, pleiotropy specifically focuses on one gene affecting multiple traits.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Pleiotropy:**

 
 
• Pleiotropic genes often encode proteins that are involved in **multiple physiological processes**. For example, hormones like **insulin** affect glucose metabolism as well as growth and development.
 
• Pleiotropy is commonly observed in **human genetic disorders**, where a mutation in a single gene can lead to a syndrome involving multiple symptoms or traits.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Pleiotropy:**
 
 
• **Sickle Cell Anemia:** A mutation in the **HBB gene** leads to abnormal hemoglobin, resulting in sickled red blood cells, anemia, and organ damage.
 
• **Marfan Syndrome:** The mutation in the **FBN1 gene** causes defects in connective tissues, affecting the skeleton, eyes, and cardiovascular system.
 
• **PKU (Phenylketonuria):** A defect in the **PAH gene** leads to an inability to metabolize phenylalanine, causing intellectual disabilities and skin pigmentation issues.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Genetics:**
 
 
• Understanding pleiotropy is essential for studying **genetic diseases**, as it provides insights into how mutations can lead to multiple health issues.
 
• Pleiotropic effects are also studied in **evolutionary biology**, as they can influence the fitness and adaptability of organisms.
 
• Research into pleiotropy helps in the development of targeted therapies for complex diseases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Polygenic Inheritance:**

 
 
• While pleiotropy involves **one gene influencing multiple traits**, polygenic inheritance involves **multiple genes contributing to a single trait.**
 
• Polygenic traits include **height, weight, and skin color**, which are determined by the combined effect of several genes.
 
 
 
• **Role in Evolutionary Biology:**
 
 
• Pleiotropy can have significant evolutionary consequences, as a mutation in a single gene can simultaneously affect multiple traits, potentially influencing an organism’s survival and reproduction.
 
• For example, a pleiotropic gene affecting both fertility and physical endurance could impact population dynamics over generations.

questions.question: How are Money Bills treated in the Houses of Parliament and State Legislatures with a bicameral system?

options.text: Rajya Sabha must approve them within 14 days
State Legislative Councils can amend them within 14 days
Both Houses have equal authority over them
Rajya Sabha and State Councils may only recommend changes within 14 days

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajya Sabha and State Councils may only recommend changes within 14 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Money Bill** is defined under **Article 110** of the **Indian Constitution**. It deals exclusively with matters like **taxation, borrowing, expenditure, or revenue collection** by the government.
 
• **Rajya Sabha's role:** The **Rajya Sabha** does not have the power to reject or amend a Money Bill. It can only provide recommendations within **14 days**. The Lok Sabha may accept or reject these recommendations. If no action is taken by the Rajya Sabha within the prescribed period, the bill is considered passed in its original form. *Hence, the statement "Rajya Sabha must approve them within 14 days" is incorrect.*
 
• **State Legislative Councils:** In states with a bicameral legislature, the **State Legislative Council** (Upper House) functions similarly to the Rajya Sabha. The Council can only recommend changes to a Money Bill and must return it to the State Legislative Assembly within **14 days**. The Assembly may accept or reject these recommendations. *Hence, the statement "State Legislative Councils can amend them within 14 days" is incorrect.*
 
• The assertion that **both Houses have equal authority** over Money Bills is incorrect. In the case of Money Bills, the **Lok Sabha** or the **State Legislative Assembly** has the final authority, and the Upper House (Rajya Sabha or Legislative Council) cannot modify or reject them. *Hence, this statement is also incorrect.*
 
• The correct treatment of a Money Bill is as follows: The **Rajya Sabha** or the **State Legislative Council** can only recommend changes to a Money Bill within **14 days**. They cannot amend or reject it. The final decision rests with the **Lok Sabha** or the **State Legislative Assembly**. *Hence, the correct answer is "Rajya Sabha and State Councils may only recommend changes within 14 days."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Money Bill Features:**

 
 
• A bill is classified as a **Money Bill** if it deals exclusively with financial matters such as **taxation, government borrowing, expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, or appropriation of funds.**
 
• The decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is made by the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha**, and this decision is final.
 
 
 
• **Procedure for Passing a Money Bill:**
 
 
• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the **Lok Sabha** or the **State Legislative Assembly** (in states with a bicameral legislature).
 
• Once passed in the **Lok Sabha**, it is sent to the **Rajya Sabha**, which may provide recommendations within 14 days. The Lok Sabha may accept or reject these recommendations.
 
• If the Rajya Sabha does not act within 14 days, the bill is deemed to have been passed in its original form by both Houses.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Money Bills:**
 
 
• The **Finance Bill**, which includes the government's annual budget proposals, is a Money Bill.
 
• Other examples include bills related to **taxation laws** and **appropriation of funds** from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Speaker:**

 
 
• The **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** has the authority to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill, and their decision is final.
 
• The Speaker's certification ensures that the **Rajya Sabha cannot delay or amend Money Bills**.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of the Upper House:**
 
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** or **State Legislative Council** cannot amend or reject a Money Bill; they may only provide recommendations.
 
• The final authority lies with the **Lok Sabha** or the **State Legislative Assembly**.

questions.question: Pushing a heavy box to start or stop its motion best demonstrates:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inertia of the object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inertia** is the property of an object to resist any change in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force. This concept is directly derived from **Newton's First Law of Motion**, also known as the Law of Inertia.
 
• When pushing a **heavy box** to either start or stop its motion, the box resists the change in its current state. If the box is initially at rest, it requires a force to overcome its inertia and set it into motion. Similarly, if the box is already moving, it requires an opposing force to bring it to rest. *Hence, this demonstrates the inertia of the object.*
 
• The larger the mass of the box, the greater its inertia. This is because inertia is directly proportional to the mass of the object. A heavier object will resist changes in its motion more than a lighter one.
 
• The other options are not directly related to the scenario described in the question:
 
 
• **Power output:** This refers to the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. While pushing a box involves applying force and doing work, the question specifically focuses on the resistance to motion, which is caused by inertia.
 
• **Conservation of energy:** This principle states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed. It is not directly demonstrated in the given scenario.
 
• **Newton's Third Law:** This law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. While this law is always at play in any physical interaction, the primary concept highlighted in the question is the resistance to motion, which is related to inertia.
 
 
 
• Thus, pushing a heavy box to start or stop its motion best demonstrates the concept of **inertia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Inertia:**

 
 
• Inertia is a fundamental property of matter. It is the tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion or rest. If an object is at rest, it will remain at rest unless acted upon by an external force. Similarly, if an object is in motion, it will continue moving at a constant velocity unless a force is applied to change its state.
 
• Inertia is directly proportional to the **mass** of an object. An object with more mass has greater inertia and requires a larger force to change its motion compared to a lighter object.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**
 
 
• **Newton's First Law:** Also known as the Law of Inertia, it states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. This law explains why a heavy box resists changes in its state of motion.
 
• **Newton's Second Law:** It relates the force applied on an object to its mass and acceleration. The formula is expressed as F = ma. The greater the mass, the more force is needed to move or stop an object.
 
• **Newton's Third Law:** For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. While pushing the box, the force applied by the person is met with an equal and opposite force from the box. However, this is not the primary concept in the given question.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Inertia:**
 
 
• Inertia is observed in daily life, such as when passengers lurch forward in a car that suddenly stops, which is due to their body trying to maintain its state of motion.
 
• Objects in space continue moving in the same direction unless acted upon by another force, demonstrating the concept of inertia on a cosmic scale.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Inertia:**

 
 
• Objects with greater mass have higher inertia, meaning they require more force to change their state of motion or rest.
 
• Inertia can be categorized into three types: **inertia of rest** (resistance to starting motion), **inertia of motion** (resistance to stopping motion), and **inertia of direction** (resistance to changing direction).
 
 
 
• **Practical Examples:**
 
 
• A train requires a longer distance to stop because of its large mass and high inertia.
 
• A ball rolling on the ground comes to a stop due to external forces like friction and air resistance, which work against its inertia of motion.
 
• A book placed on a table remains stationary unless a force is applied to move it, demonstrating inertia of rest.

questions.question: The Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita (BNS), 2023, consolidates and updates which area of law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Criminal substantive law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita (BNS), 2023**, is aimed at reforming and modernizing the criminal laws of India.
 
• The BNS focuses on consolidating and updating **criminal substantive law**, which governs offenses and prescribes penalties.
 
• It seeks to replace the existing **Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860**, which has been the cornerstone of criminal law in India for over 160 years. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The BNS introduces new provisions for crimes and penalties, aligning with modern societal and technological changes, such as cybercrime and human trafficking.
 
• It also seeks to simplify legal language and improve clarity in the law, making it more accessible to citizens and legal practitioners alike. *This supports the correct answer.*
 
• **Evidence-related rules**, civil procedural matters, and contractual obligations are governed by separate laws, such as the **Indian Evidence Act, 1872**, **Civil Procedure Code (CPC), 1908**, and **Indian Contract Act, 1872**, respectively. These areas are not directly addressed by the BNS. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is Criminal substantive law.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita (BNS), 2023:**

 
 
• **BNS** is part of the Indian government's initiative to overhaul colonial-era laws, such as the **Indian Penal Code (IPC), Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), and Indian Evidence Act.**
 
• The focus is on creating a legal framework that reflects the evolving needs of society and incorporates advancements in technology and global legal standards.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Criminal Substantive Law:**
 
 
• Criminal substantive law defines offenses such as theft, murder, and fraud, along with prescribing punishments for these offenses.
 
• It ensures justice by balancing the rights of the accused and the victim.
 
• **Example:** Sections of the IPC define crimes like **Section 302 (Punishment for Murder)** and **Section 376 (Punishment for Rape).**
 
 
 
• **Modernization in Criminal Law:**
 
 
• The BNS aims to address emerging crimes, such as **cybercrime, financial fraud, and terrorism**, that were not adequately covered under the IPC.
 
• It incorporates provisions for **victim compensation** and emphasizes the principles of restorative justice.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Substantive and Procedural Law:**

 
 
• **Substantive law** deals with the rights and duties of individuals and the punishments for crimes.
 
• **Procedural law**, such as the **CrPC**, outlines the steps for the enforcement of substantive law, including investigation and trial processes.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of the Indian Evidence Act:**
 
 
• The **Indian Evidence Act, 1872**, governs the admissibility of evidence in judicial proceedings.
 
• It is separate from substantive criminal law and is not directly part of the BNS.

__
 
• **Oxygen concentration in Earth's atmosphere:** The Earth's atmosphere contains approximately **21%** oxygen, which is represented as **0.21** in decimal form. This is the correct and scientifically proven value.
 
• Oxygen is essential for the survival of most living organisms on Earth, as it is a critical component in cellular respiration. This atmospheric concentration is suitable for sustaining life.
 
• The Earth's atmosphere is predominantly composed of **nitrogen (78%)** and **oxygen (21%)**, with other gases such as **argon (0.93%)**, **carbon dioxide (0.04%)**, and trace amounts of other gases. *Hence, option 0.21 is correct.*
 
• **Scientific evidence:** The concentration of oxygen has been measured consistently over centuries and has remained stable at approximately **21%**, making this value accurate and reliable.
 
• None of the other options (0.18, 0.24, or 0.28) correspond to the actual oxygen concentration in the atmosphere. These values are either too low or too high, which could disrupt life-sustaining processes. *Hence, the correct answer is 0.21.*

• The Earth's atmosphere is a mixture of gases, primarily composed of **nitrogen (78%)** and **oxygen (21%)**. This balance is crucial for sustaining life and maintaining ecological balance.
 
• Other components include **argon (0.93%)**, **carbon dioxide (0.04%)**, water vapor, and trace gases such as neon, helium, methane, and krypton.
 
• Trace gases play a significant role in processes like the greenhouse effect and atmospheric chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Oxygen:**
 
 
• Oxygen supports **cellular respiration**, a process through which organisms convert glucose into energy. This energy is vital for metabolic activities.
 
• It is also a key component in the formation of the ozone layer, which protects Earth from harmful **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**.
 
• The stable concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere ensures a balance in breathing and combustion processes.
 
 
 
• **Historical Evolution:**
 
 
• The Earth's atmosphere has evolved over billions of years. Initially, it lacked oxygen, but with the advent of **photosynthetic organisms**, oxygen levels increased, enabling the development of complex life forms.
 
• The **Great Oxygenation Event**, which occurred approximately 2.5 billion years ago, marked a significant increase in atmospheric oxygen.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:

1. The Supreme Court can transfer a case from one High Court to another.

2. Article 139A was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment.

Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** The Supreme Court can transfer a case from one High Court to another.

 
 
• This power of the Supreme Court is derived from **Article 139A(2)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It allows the Supreme Court to transfer cases from one High Court to another if it is in the interest of justice or if the cases involve similar issues requiring a unified decision.
 
• The Supreme Court exercises this power to avoid conflicting judgments across High Courts on the same subject matter and to ensure judicial consistency. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** Article 139A was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment.
 
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, also known as the "Mini Constitution," introduced **Article 139A** to the Constitution.
 
• This Article empowers the Supreme Court to transfer cases involving the same or substantially the same questions of law, which are pending before different High Courts, to itself or to one High Court for a decision.
 
• The addition of this Article aimed to strengthen the unity of the judicial system and prevent contradictory rulings by different High Courts. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both 1 and 2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 139A of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Clause (1):** It enables the Supreme Court to withdraw cases pending before one or more High Courts if they involve the same or substantially similar questions of law. The Supreme Court can decide these cases itself.
 
• **Clause (2):** It authorizes the Supreme Court to transfer cases from one High Court to another in the interest of justice or to avoid conflicting judgments.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• This amendment is one of the most comprehensive amendments to the Indian Constitution, also called the "Mini Constitution."
 
• Besides adding **Article 139A**, it also brought significant changes to the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles of State Policy, and the powers of the judiciary and executive.
 
• It aimed to strengthen the central government's authority and bring uniformity in judicial decisions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Judicial Transfer of Cases:**
 
 
• The transfer of cases ensures uniformity in judicial decisions across different High Courts.
 
• It prevents conflicting judgments on the same subject matter, which could cause confusion and weaken the legal system.
 
• This power is often used in cases involving constitutional interpretation, inter-state disputes, or matters of national importance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judicial Precedents on Article 139A:**

 
 
• The Supreme Court has invoked Article 139A in cases that involve similar legal issues being heard in multiple High Courts, such as tax disputes, inter-state water disputes, or constitutional interpretation.
 
• Example: In the **Ayodhya Land Dispute**, the Supreme Court consolidated multiple cases from various courts to ensure a uniform verdict.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Judiciary:**
 
 
• The judiciary acts as the guardian of the Constitution and ensures uniformity in the interpretation and application of laws across the country.
 
• Through Articles like 139A, the judiciary maintains consistency and avoids ambiguity in legal principles.

Had I known about the traffic, I __will leave early.__
questions.solution:

__
 
• The sentence uses a **third conditional structure**, which is used to talk about unreal past situations and their possible results.
 
• The structure of the third conditional is:

 **Had + past participle, would have + past participle**.
 
• The highlighted part **“I will leave early”** is incorrect because “will” cannot be used for unreal past conditions.
 
• The correct replacement is **“would have left earlier”**, which fits the required conditional rule.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Had I known about the traffic, I **would have left earlier**."*

• **Option 2: would leave early** – Incorrect because it is used for second conditional (present unreal), not past unreal.
 
• **Option 3: had left earlier** – Incorrect because it forms a wrong clause combination and breaks the conditional structure.
 
• **Option 4: would left earlier** – Grammatically incorrect since “would” must be followed by the base form (leave), not “left”.
